title: Innovative Approach To Human-IoT Interaction Using Weak AI Models
content: The aim of this study is to explore and validate the potential of using brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and electroencephalography (EEG) signals to control external devices, specifically unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The main problem of research is to integrate between human cognitive functions with Internet of things (IoT) devices, enabling hands-free control based on mental commands. Such an approach could transform fields where rapid, precise, and intuitive control is critical, including healthcare, search-and-rescue missions, and industrial automation. By capturing raw EEG data associated with simple motor commands, we demonstrate the feasibility of translating specific brainwave patterns into UAV instructions like "hover" and "land." The next phase will involve analog-to-digital processing and filtering to refine these signals, preparing them for machine learning algorithms to enhance command accuracy. Our findings highlight the promise of neural interfaces as a bridge between human thought and machine action, paving the way for advancements in IoT-based human-technology interaction.
